message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: Lint
on:
  push:

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-22.04
    timeout-minutes: 5
    strategy:
      matrix:
        node-version: [20]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Install pnpm and Node.js ${{ matrix.node-version }}
        uses: pnpm/setup@v3
        with:
          runtime: node@${{ matrix.node-version }}
          cache: true
          require-lockfile: true
      - name: Run check
        run: pnpm check",
  "rationale": "The P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT pattern is supported by measured CI workflow evidence (experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508) showing 26.8% elapsed savings from adding a job timeout, and the pattern's reported result. The repository has representative successful-duration history (recent runs complete in roughly 23-33 seconds), so a 5-minute bound provides ample headroom without risking valid slow runs. Dependency caching already exists via pnpm/setup@v3 cache: true, so P-LIT-GHA-CACHE is contraindicated, and the single-cell matrix makes P-LIT-FAIL-FAST ineffective. Adding timeout-minutes preserves the required check and coverage, adds no privileges, secrets, publishing/deployment operations, or new network access, and only bounds runaway job consumption.",
  "evidence_ids": ["experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508", "pattern:P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT"]
}
